issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may intervene at an interlocutory stage when declining to do so risks irreparable injustice.
material_facts: The tenant appealed after the refusal to stay an eviction suit pending determination of the tenant’s earlier rent-fixation application.
If the eviction suit proceeded and resulted in eviction, the rent-fixation application could become infructuous.
issues.conclusion: The Court intervened at the interlocutory stage because a hands-off approach risked irreparable injustice.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that although it is reluctant to interfere at an interlocutory stage, it may do so where declining to intervene could cause irreparable injustice. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.

predicates.interlocutory_appeal_from_refusal: A party brought an interlocutory appeal after a court refused to pause a proceeding.
predicates.nonintervention_risks_irreparable_injust: If the challenged refusal stands, the party’s pending application may become ineffective before it is decided.

issues.definition: When a party brings an interlocutory appeal from a refusal and nonintervention risks irreparable injustice, the court intervenes at the interlocutory stage.

issues.legal_issue: An eviction suit should be stayed when a prior rent-fixation application may determine statutory tenant protection and proceeding with the suit could defeat that application.
material_facts: The tenant filed a rent-fixation application before the landlord filed the eviction suit.
The fair-rent determination could affect whether the tenant qualified for protection under the Karnataka Rent Control Act, 1961, and therefore could affect the eviction suit.
If the eviction suit proceeded to eviction before the rent-fixation application was decided, that application could become infructuous.
The landlord expressed concern that staying the suit could cause lengthy delay in its resolution.
issues.conclusion: The Court stayed further proceedings in the eviction suit and directed that the rent-fixation application receive top priority and be disposed of as early as possible, within four months. The Court relied on the parties’ agreement about the rent threshold for protection under the Karnataka Rent Control Act, 1961; it cited no particular statutory provision or earlier case.
issues.legal_principle: Balancing the equities, a court should preserve a prior rent-fixation application where its determination may affect the eviction suit and allowing the suit to proceed could render the application infructuous. Concern about delay may be addressed by directing priority and prompt determination of the application.

predicates.interlocutory_appeal_from_refusal: A party brought an interlocutory appeal after a court refused to pause an eviction suit.
predicates.prior_rent_fixation_application: The tenant applied to have rent fixed before the landlord filed the eviction suit.
predicates.rent_determination_could_affect_eviction: The rent determination could affect whether the tenant is entitled to statutory protection relevant to the eviction suit.
predicates.eviction_suit_could_render_application_i: The eviction suit could proceed to eviction before the rent-fixation application is decided, making that application ineffective.

issues.definition: When an interlocutory appeal concerns refusal to pause an eviction suit, and a prior rent-fixation application could affect the suit but be defeated by its continuation, the suit is stayed and the rent determination is expedited.
